title: MS-108: Observable Golf Outputs, Impact Semantics and Accuracy Budgets
body:
## Objective
Ensure marker fit quality supports useful and defensible golf outputs instead of hiding critical errors in whole-body RMS.

## Scope and Deliverables
- Specify clubhead position/speed/path, face orientation, impact timing, pelvis/torso sequencing and any advertised joint-load outputs with units, frames, phase windows, filtering/time alignment and error budgets tied to intended use.
- Audit marker/club calibration observability, especially club axial rotation/face angle with sparse or collinear club markers. Unobservable outputs remain unavailable or uncertainty-qualified; add explicit calibration/marker acquisition requirements rather than inventing values.
- Separate tracking through an impact timestamp from a physical ball-strike model. If physical impact/ball-flight claims are offered, create bounded dependent model/validation tasks for measured ball/club conditions and collision parameters; do not mark impact physics validated by C3D pose tracking.
- Define phase-specific and peak/percentile errors, coverage and independent comparison against calibrated reference instruments when available. No acceptance threshold relaxation based solely on the current fitted trial.
- Integrate metric metadata and confidence into existing receipts, viewer and exported report. Preserve canonical time rather than unconstrained time warping that conceals event errors.

## Acceptance Tests
Synthetic observable/unobservable club configurations; missing/gapped club markers; known event offsets; held-out reference comparisons. UI/export never displays precise validated face/load/impact outputs without supporting calibration and evidence.

## Dependencies and Ownership
MS-100 and MS-90 phase-A data audit; protocol coordination with MS-101 but no dependency on its final report. Accountable role: golf biomechanics/product metrics lead. Feeds MS-101 and MS-106.

## Execution and Evidence Contract
Part of epic #10363; owner-authorized contract revision 2026-09-17. This issue is planning, not evidence of implementation or qualification.
Before implementation, check/post the existing issue lease and register presence through Repository_Management; preserve existing owners and worktrees. Use the established source modules, candidate/receipt schemas, feature-parity and industrial-readiness registries. No parallel metrics or acceptance authority.
Use focused topic PRs with issue references, repo-standard validation, relevant native-engine tests, and negative-path tests. Mocks or skipped native tests cannot qualify a native engine. Update the canonical handoff and the existing governing-issue development-log row in place. Store content-addressed evidence with source/model/data/runtime/contract hashes; keep historical evidence immutable and mark superseded verdicts explicitly. Workflow changes follow the Repository_Management fleet campaign process.
The program coordinator allocates a lease holder before implementation; the accountable role below is not a claim that an agent has accepted the task. Release remains blocked until the linked evidence passes the revised contracts.

## Program Qualification Dependencies
- MS-100 (#10374): Fail-Closed Metrics and Versioned Physical Acceptance Qualification
- MS-101 (#10375): Independent Scientific Validation, Identifiability and Uncertainty
- MS-106 (#10380): Professional Release Gate and Both-Shell Customer Qualification
